sections.heading: B — Signals, roundabouts, railroads and markings
sections.markdown:
## B — Signals, roundabouts, railroads and markings
Audience: first-time Montana non-commercial Class D applicants studying signals, roundabouts, railroads and markings.
Level: introductory rule retrieval; the ordered handbook section is the coverage basis, without any invented official examination weight. Prerequisites and confusable topics: The previous section on signs, work zones and school zones; the distinction between steady and flashing signal displays, and between white same-direction and yellow opposing-traffic lane lines.
This is a research handoff. Read physical pages forty through forty-five as ordinary signal, roundabout, railroad and marking guidance. Signal-head diagrams are carried only through the extracted text descriptions. Posted lane controls that vary by time or place remain debt until the displayed control is confirmed.

sections.heading: C — Signals, roundabouts, railroads and markings
sections.markdown:
## C — Signals, roundabouts, railroads and markings

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic signals direct vehicles and pedestrians at certain intersections and mid-block crosswalks by assigning the right of way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
A signal that is not working is treated like stop signs in every direction, with the driver who stops first going first while staying cautious. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Where pedestrian signals are used, walkers obey them instead of the vehicle lights, and a WALK display lets them start crossing from the curb or sidewalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
A steady or flashing DON’T WALK display means wait for WALK, while walkers already in the crosswalk keep crossing; an orange hand means DON’T WALK and a white figure means WALK. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
A steady red light means stop before the stop line, the crosswalk, or the intersection, then a cautious right turn is allowed unless a sign or officer forbids it, yielding to pedestrians, bicyclists and traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street after stopping, and pedestrians facing red must stay out of the street unless a pedestrian signal directs otherwise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
A steady red arrow means stop and remain stopped except for the allowed turns on red. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
A flashing red light works like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, look left, right and ahead, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and continue when safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow light warns that red is next, so enter cautiously and only when too close to stop safely, while pedestrians facing yellow must not start across. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow arrow ends the protected turn interval, so turning vehicles clear the intersection and prepare to obey the next display. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
A flashing yellow arrow permits a left turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, who hold the green, and only when a safe gap exists. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution, which usually calls for slowing down. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
A steady green light means go with caution while watching for traffic running the red, and pedestrians facing green may cross in a marked or unmarked crosswalk unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A02
A steady green arrow grants a protected turning movement, while turning traffic without a green arrow is unprotected and yields to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A03
Roundabout driving speeds are fifteen miles per hour or less, so slow down on approach. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A03
Yield to vehicles already inside the roundabout because they hold the right-of-way, and remember that circulation runs counterclockwise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A03
Enter to the right of the center island and keep moving when the way is clear, and never pass another vehicle inside a single-lane roundabout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A03
Circle to the desired street, give a right-turn signal, and exit, yielding to pedestrians who are in or waiting at the crosswalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A03
Give large vehicles extra room because their rear wheels track over the sloped truck apron, so a smaller vehicle should drop back behind them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians cross only at the marked crosswalks and never walk to the central island, staying cautious even though vehicles must stop for them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A03
Bicyclists are urged to walk their bicycles on the sidewalks and crosswalks, or to ride the circulatory roadway as a vehicle with clear turn signals. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A03
When an emergency vehicle approaches, never stop inside the roundabout; exit normally and then pull right, or pull over before entering only where room allows. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A04
Never race a train to the crossing, stop whenever safety is in doubt, keep space for the vehicle on the far side, and avoid shifting gears on the tracks. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A04
Stop as close as practical but at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail when signals, gates, signs, watchmen, an approaching train, or a plainly hazardous visible train within fifteen hundred feet requires it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A04
Advance warning signs placed before the crossing order drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A04
Railroad pavement markings with a stop line, an X and the letters RR warn that a crossing lies ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A04
Crossbuck signs stand at every public crossing, with a lower sign giving the track count where more than one track exists, and drivers stay ready to stop for a train. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A04
Always stop when the crossing lights start to flash, and where several tracks exist confirm that every track is clear before crossing. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A04
At gated crossings stop when the lights flash before the gates fall, and remain stopped until the gates rise and the flashing ends. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A05
A broken yellow centerline may be crossed, but only to overtake or pass another vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A05
A solid yellow line on the driver side bars passing over the centerline, a double yellow line bars crossing from either direction, and a solid centerline may be crossed only within a left turn. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A05
Lane lines are white between traffic moving the same way and yellow between opposing traffic, while solid edge lines mark the road edge. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A05
A dashed white lane line allows a careful lane change, while a solid white lane line means stay in lane except in a special situation. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A05
When a sign or signal requires a stop, halt before the stop line or crosswalk and yield to pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk, whether marked or not. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A05
A dashed yellow line between opposing lanes allows passing when safe, a solid-plus-dashed pair allows passing only when the dashed line is on the driver side, and two solid lines bar passing for both sides. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A05
A solid yellow line may be crossed to turn into a parking lot, driveway or roadway when it is safe to do so. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A06
Reversible lanes change direction by time of day, are usually marked with double-dashed yellow lines, and require checking the signs or overhead lights before use. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A06
Over a reversible lane a green arrow allows use, a red X forbids it, a flashing yellow X allows turning only, and a steady yellow X orders leaving the lane as soon as safely possible. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A06
Reserved lanes carry signed special uses and often a white diamond, with transit or bus lanes limited to buses and bicycle lanes limited to bicycles. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A06
High-occupancy lanes require the signed minimum number of people aboard during the posted days and hours, so an HOV three marking demands at least three occupants. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A06
A shared center lane serves left turns from both directions, plus U-turns where allowed, and is marked on each side by a solid-plus-dashed yellow pair. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A06
Where no signs or lane markings control lane use, the default rules for driving, passing and turning decide the lane. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

Misconceptions: A flashing red is a stop, not a yield; a plain green never protects a turn the way a green arrow does.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: color first, then arrow or shape, then yield before moving.
Glossary: Protected turn; unprotected turn; truck apron; crossbuck; shared center lane; reversible lane; stop line.
Dynamic facts: Posted reversible-lane signals and local lane reservations change by time and place; obey the displayed control.

sections.heading: C2 — Signals, roundabouts, railroads and markings
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Signals, roundabouts, railroads and markings

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
A dead signal and a flashing red light both demand a stop-sign style stop, while a flashing yellow light on the same page asks only for cautious movement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
Pedestrian WALK and DON’T WALK displays overrule the vehicle lights for walkers, so a green vehicle light never releases a pedestrian who faces DON’T WALK. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
A right turn on red is broadly allowed after stopping, while a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A01
A steady red arrow requires stopping and remaining stopped except for the handbook’s allowed turns on red; a flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding and proceeding only when safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow arrow closes an existing protected turn, while a flashing yellow arrow opens an unprotected left turn that must yield to oncoming traffic holding the green. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow light only urges caution and slower movement, while a steady green light grants movement with continued watch for traffic running the red. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A02
A green arrow protects the indicated turning movement, while a plain green ball leaves turning traffic unprotected and yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A03
Traffic already circulating inside a roundabout holds the right-of-way over entering traffic, reversing the first-arrived expectation of an all-way stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A03
Passing is forbidden inside a single-lane roundabout, while the ordinary passing rules continue to govern the roads outside the circle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A03
An approaching emergency vehicle is met by exiting the roundabout first and pulling over after, never by stopping inside the circle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A04
Advance warning signs only urge readiness to stop at the crossing ahead, while flashing crossing lights and lowered gates order an actual stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A04
Flashing-light signals order stopping as soon as the flashing starts, while gates add a barrier that must fully rise with the flashing ended before traffic resumes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A05
White lines divide lanes of traffic moving the same way, while yellow lines divide opposing traffic, so the color alone reveals the traffic pattern. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A05
A solid-plus-dashed yellow pair permits passing only from the dashed side, while two solid yellow lines forbid passing from both directions. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A05
A stop line marks where vehicles halt for a sign or signal, while a crosswalk marks where pedestrians cross and hold priority over vehicles. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A06
Reserved lanes restrict use to the signed vehicle types during posted times, while reversible lanes change their allowed direction of travel by time of day. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A06
A shared center lane permits left turns from either direction, while a reversible lane carries through traffic in its currently authorized direction. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A06
A flashing yellow X over a reversible lane allows turning movements only, while a steady yellow X orders drivers to vacate the lane as soon as safely possible. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0045]
